chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
A man complained to the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) of loneliness, and he ordered him to take a pair of pigeons in his house.

key_terms.الوحشة: Loneliness, desolation, the feeling of emptiness and isolation
key_terms.زوج حمام: A pair of pigeons — prescribed as a remedy for loneliness

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet prescribe as a remedy for loneliness?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) prescribed keeping a pair of pigeons as a remedy for loneliness. This hadith reflects the prophetic concern for emotional well-being and the companionship found in keeping birds. In early Islamic culture, pigeons were prized household companions, and their cooing was considered to bring a sense of comfort and aliveness to an otherwise empty home.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqan, from Dorost, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A man complained to Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> of loneliness, so he<sup>saww</sup> ordered him to take in his house, a pair of pigeons’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ‘Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan from Durust from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once

a man complained before the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, about loneliness and fear. He (the Messenger of Allah) commanded him to keep a pair of pigeons in his house.’”
